findings.claim: In addGuests.handler.ts, the team permission check uses `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)` where `||` is intended. This reduces it to an owner-only check, so team ADMINs who are not the organizer or an attendee get FORBIDDEN even though the variable is named isTeamAdminOrOwner.

verifier.reason: addGuests.handler.ts (patch lines 470-472) sets isTeamAdminOrOwner to `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`. isTeamAdmin already matches both ADMIN and OWNER (packages/lib/server/queries/teams/index.ts:270), while isTeamOwner matches only OWNER (:292), so the combined check passes only for owners. A team ADMIN who is neither the organizer nor an attendee hits the FORBIDDEN branch at line 478.

findings.claim: The BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS check lowercases the blacklist but compares it against the raw guest email, with no toLowerCase or extractBaseEmail normalization. Blacklisted addresses therefore pass when submitted with different casing or a plus-alias.

verifier.reason: addGuests.handler.ts:70-72 lowercases the BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS entries, but line 77 checks them with `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` against the raw guest string, with no toLowerCase or extractBaseEmail. A differently cased or plus-aliased address therefore gets past the blacklist, whereas handleNewBooking.ts:742 normalizes with `extractBaseEmail(guest).toLowerCase()`.

findings.claim: De-duplication against existing booking attendees is case-sensitive, so `A@x.com` can be added next to an existing `a@x.com`.

verifier.reason: addGuests.handler.ts (patch line 500) filters with a strict `guest === attendee.email`, and the input schema (addGuests.schema.ts) is only `z.string().email()`, with no lowercasing. So `A@x.com` passes the filter next to an existing `a@x.com` and gets inserted by `createMany`. The client check (AddGuestsDialog `new Set(emails)`) and the blacklist check, which lowercases only the blacklist entries, are case-sensitive too.

findings.claim: The server does not de-duplicate the input guests array (uniqueGuests only filters existing attendees and the blacklist). A direct tRPC call with repeated emails creates duplicate attendee rows and sends duplicate emails, and there is no unique constraint on (bookingId, email) and no server-side cap on list size.

verifier.reason: The server schema accepts any array of emails, with no uniqueness check and no `.max()` (addGuests.schema.ts:609). The `uniqueGuests` filter only removes existing attendees and blacklisted addresses (addGuests.handler.ts:498-502), so repeated emails each get their own row through `createMany` (handler:516-530), and `sendAddGuestsEmails` emails every one of those rows. The Attendee model has only `@@index([email])` and `@@index([bookingId])`, with no unique constraint on (bookingId, email) (packages/prisma/schema.prisma:526-539). The duplicate check exists only in the client dialog (AddGuestsDialog.tsx:79-82).

findings.claim: The handler passes the raw `guests` input to sendAddGuestsEmails instead of `uniqueGuests`. As a result, existing or filtered attendees are classified as new and receive the wrong email (AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of AttendeeAddGuestsEmail), and notifications go to guests who were not actually added.

verifier.reason: addGuests.handler.ts (patch line 592) calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the raw input instead of `uniqueGuests` (line 498). sendAddGuestsEmails (emails/email-manager.ts, patch line 234) uses `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` to pick the template, so an existing attendee repeated in the input gets AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of AttendeeAddGuestsEmail. One part of the claim is wrong: emails are only sent to `calEvent.attendees`, so blacklisted guests that were never added get no email.

findings.claim: sendAddGuestsEmails does not check the event type's disableStandardEmails settings, and the handler does not pass booking.eventType?.metadata. Emails are therefore sent even when standard host/attendee emails are disabled.

verifier.reason: The new sendAddGuestsEmails in packages/emails/email-manager.ts (patch lines 218-243) only takes (calEvent, newGuests) and sends organizer, team-member and attendee emails without any check. That differs from sendLocationChangeEmails just above it (email-manager.ts:503,515), which checks eventTypeDisableHostEmail/eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail. addGuests.handler.ts calls sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) without booking.eventType?.metadata (patch line 592).

findings.claim: sendAddGuestsEmails does not respect the hideCalendarNotes setting, so hidden notes can be sent to attendees.

verifier.reason: sendAddGuestsEmails (packages/emails/email-manager.ts:525-550 after the patch) sends AttendeeScheduledEmail and AttendeeAddGuestsEmail to every attendee without the `hideCalendarNotes && { additionalNotes: undefined }` stripping used at email-manager.ts:119 and 267. The addGuests handler also never reads eventType.hideCalendarNotes and puts booking.description, where the booker's additional notes are stored (createBooking.ts:212), into evt.description, which BaseScheduledEmail.tsx:87 renders, so hidden notes reach both old attendees and new guests.

findings.claim: `props` is spread after the fixed template props, so callers can override the email's subject, title and header.

verifier.reason: The claim is accurate but harmless. In packages/emails/src/templates/AttendeeAddGuestsEmail.tsx:5-8 and OrganizerAddGuestsEmail.tsx:5-9, title, headerType and subject are set first and `{...props}` comes last, so a caller could override them. The only callers (attendee-add-guests-email.ts:323-326 and organizer-add-guests-email.ts:367-370) pass just calEvent and attendee, and the existing templates (e.g. AttendeeLocationChangeEmail.tsx:5-8) follow the same default-then-override pattern.

findings.claim: New guests are saved with an empty name and inherit the organizer's timeZone/locale, so emails and calendar entries show blank names.

verifier.reason: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:507-514 (patch lines 507-514) builds each new guest as {name: "", email, timeZone: organizer.timeZone, locale: organizer.locale} and saves it with createMany. Those blank names then reach the emails, e.g. the attendee `to:` field in attendee-add-guests-email.ts, and the calendar update through updateCalendarAttendees. Guests added at booking time also get an empty name, so this follows existing practice, but the claim is accurate.

findings.claim: In the add-guests dialog, isInvalidEmail is not reset on success or on overlay/Esc close, so the error state can reappear when the dialog is reopened. Closing via onOpenChange also keeps the old emails, removing all fields makes Add a silent no-op, and the client uniqueness check is case-sensitive.

verifier.reason: In apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx, onSuccess (patch L89-94) resets the emails but not isInvalidEmail, and onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog} (L114) clears neither the emails nor the error; since the dialog stays mounted in BookingListItem, both come back when it is reopened. Also, handleAdd returns silently when the list is empty (L102-104), and the uniqueness check uses a plain `new Set(emails)` (L79-82), so it is case-sensitive.

findings.claim: The invalid-email banner stays visible after the user edits the input to valid values. It clears only on Cancel or on another add attempt.

verifier.reason: In apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx, isInvalidEmail is set to true in handleAdd (line ~57). The MultiEmail setValue (line ~74) only updates multiEmailValue, so editing the input never clears the banner. The claim overstates how it clears: the only setIsInvalidEmail(false) is in the Cancel handler (line ~92), and handleAdd never resets it, so a later valid add attempt does not clear it either and it can reappear when the dialog is reopened.

findings.claim: MultiEmail contains an empty fragment `<></>` in a conditional.

verifier.reason: packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx:73-75 uses `) : (<></>)` as the else branch of the `value.length ?` ternary. The patch adds this new file. The fragment works but is redundant; `null` or `&&` would do the same job.

findings.claim: No tests are included for the new addGuests handler/mutation or the new UI components.

verifier.reason: The patch changes only source files: BookingListItem.tsx, AddGuestsDialog.tsx, the email templates, addGuests.handler.ts, addGuests.schema.ts, MultiEmail.tsx and MultiEmailLazy.tsx. It adds no test or spec files, and no test file in the repo mentions addGuests, AddGuestsDialog or MultiEmail.

findings.claim: The server does not check booking status or time. Guests can be added to CANCELLED, REJECTED or past bookings, which writes attendee rows and sends REQUEST/CONFIRMED ICS invites.

verifier.reason: addGuests.handler.ts (patch lines 450-592) loads the booking by id and checks only who the user is (admin/owner, organizer or attendee). It never checks booking.status or startTime/endTime. It then adds attendee rows with prisma.booking.update and calls sendAddGuestsEmails, which sends REQUEST/CONFIRMED ICS files (attendee-add-guests-email.ts:304-313). The UI hides the action for non-upcoming bookings (BookingListItem.tsx:544), but anyone allowed to call the endpoint directly can still do this.

findings.claim: MultiEmail is a near-verbatim copy of the multiemail factory in packages/features/form-builder/Components.tsx.

verifier.reason: The new packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx:630-712 copies the `multiemail` factory at packages/features/form-builder/Components.tsx:234-313 almost line for line: same class string, same EmailField/Tooltip/Button layout and same add/remove logic. It differs only in copying the array before updating it, plus the test IDs and the label's htmlFor/class. The original still carries the comment `//TODO: Make it a ui component` and was not changed to use the new component.

findings.claim: In onError, the toast message is the template string `${code}: ${t(msg)}`, which is never falsy. The unable_to_add_guests fallback is therefore never used, and users see raw 'CODE: key' strings.

verifier.reason: In the patch's onError (change.patch lines 96-97), `message` is the template literal `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`. A template literal always contains at least ": ", so it is never empty and `t("unable_to_add_guests")` can never be used. The server throws the key `you_do_not_have_permission` (patch line 479), but en/common.json has no such key, so the user sees a raw string like 'FORBIDDEN: you_do_not_have_permission'.

findings.claim: The email list state starts as an array containing an empty string rather than an empty array.

verifier.reason: apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:32 initialises the list with `useState<string[]>([""])`, and lines 39 and 90 reset it to `[""]` again. Because of this, the `multiEmailValue.length === 0` guard in handleAdd (line 49) never fires on the initial state, so clicking Add with nothing typed shows the 'emails must be unique and valid' error instead of doing nothing.

findings.claim: evt is built without `team`, so the team-member branch in sendAddGuestsEmails never runs and team hosts are not notified.

verifier.reason: The CalendarEvent built in addGuests.handler.ts (patch lines 548-571) has no `team` field, so the `calendarEvent.team?.members` loop in sendAddGuestsEmails (email-manager.ts, patch lines 224-230) never runs. Only the organizer and the attendees get emails; other team hosts on collective bookings get nothing.

findings.claim: showAttendees is not passed to AttendeeScheduledEmail, so seated events with seatsShowAttendees=true hide the attendee list in these emails.

verifier.reason: In packages/emails/email-manager.ts (the new sendAddGuestsEmails, patch lines 235/237), both AttendeeScheduledEmail and AttendeeAddGuestsEmail are built as (calendarEvent, attendee) with no third argument. The constructor at attendee-scheduled-email.ts:21 then trims attendees down to the recipient whenever calEvent.seatsPerTimeSlot is set, even though addGuests.handler.ts sets seatsShowAttendees on evt.

findings.claim: There is no seated-event handling: attendee rows are created without BookingSeat rows, which bypasses seatsPerTimeSlot. The full attendee list is pushed to the calendar event, and any seat-holder can add guests, exposing seat-holders to each other even when seatsShowAttendees is false.

verifier.reason: addGuests.handler.ts:516-530 uses createMany to add attendees with no bookingSeat. createNewSeat.ts:52 only counts attendees that have a bookingSeat, so these guests sidestep seatsPerTimeSlot. The isAttendee check at handler:476 lets any seat-holder add guests, and the full attendee list goes to updateCalendarAttendees (handler:589). The exposure part is overstated: the emails cut the list down to the recipient (attendee-scheduled-email.ts:21), and Google applies seatsShowAttendees (googlecalendar CalendarService.ts:413), so only other calendar providers could leak the list.

findings.claim: The new action updates by bookingId only, without seat-level scoping, so on seats events guests are added to the shared booking instead of the current seat.

verifier.reason: BookingListItem.tsx has the seat context (`booking.seatsReferences`, used at lines 134-138), but the patch passes only `bookingId={booking.id}` to AddGuestsDialog. The new addGuests.handler.ts then runs `prisma.booking.update({ where: { id: bookingId }, data: { attendees: { createMany } } })` with no BookingSeat link or seat check, so on seated events the guests become seatless attendees of the shared booking.

findings.claim: The booking findFirst include pulls user.credentials (full credential keys), which are never read, and trips @calcom/eslint/no-prisma-include-true.

verifier.reason: In addGuests.handler.ts (patch lines 450-466), the booking `findFirst` includes `user: { include: { destinationCalendar: true, credentials: true } }`, but `booking.user.credentials` is never read: EventManager gets its credentials from `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` (patch line 582), and `updateCalendarAttendees` only uses `PartialBooking` (id/userId/references). The rule in packages/eslint-plugin/src/rules/no-prisma-include-true.ts:27-44 searches nested `include` blocks and flags `credentials: true`, though recommended.ts:9 sets the rule to only warn.

findings.claim: addGuests uses plain authedProcedure with a custom check instead of bookingsProcedure. Any logged-in attendee can add guests, while COLLECTIVE co-hosts are refused.

verifier.reason: The route does use plain authedProcedure (_router.tsx:399) with a custom check that lets any matching attendee through (addGuests.handler.ts:476-478). But COLLECTIVE co-hosts are not refused: createBooking.ts:153-161 saves team members as Attendee rows, so co-hosts pass the isAttendee check.

findings.claim: About 40 lines of CalendarEvent construction are duplicated from editLocation.handler.ts.

verifier.reason: In the new addGuests.handler.ts (patch lines 532-571), the attendee-list mapping, tOrganizer lookup and CalendarEvent object (title, type, description, start/end time, organizer, recurringEvent, destinationCalendar, seatsPerTimeSlot, seatsShowAttendees) are nearly identical to editLocation.handler.ts:55-95, about 40 lines. The only differences are the location and conferenceCredentialId fields; the claim names the wrong file, since the copy is in addGuests.handler.ts.

findings.claim: A second prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow refetches the organizer that is already loaded via booking.user.

verifier.reason: In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:35-40, `booking.user` is loaded with all its scalar fields, including name, email, timeZone and locale. Then at :58-68, `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })` fetches those same four fields again, which costs an extra database query.

findings.claim: The email uniqueness check in ZAddGuestsInputSchema is case-sensitive, so User@x.com and user@x.com pass as unique.

verifier.reason: At apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26-29, ZAddGuestsInputSchema checks uniqueness with `new Set(emails)` on the raw strings, without lowercasing, so User@x.com and user@x.com count as different. The server schema (addGuests.schema.ts:3-6) has no uniqueness check, and the handler compares guests to existing attendees case-sensitively (addGuests.handler.ts:76-79), so both addresses would be stored.

findings.claim: The handler throws FORBIDDEN with message key you_do_not_have_permission, which is not defined in en/common.json, so users see the raw key.

verifier.reason: addGuests.handler.ts:55 (patch line 479) throws FORBIDDEN with message "you_do_not_have_permission", and that key appears nowhere in apps/web/public/static/locales/en. AddGuestsDialog.tsx onError passes it through t(err.message), so the toast shows "FORBIDDEN: you_do_not_have_permission".

findings.claim: There is no transaction or compensation: attendees are written before updateCalendarAttendees, which is not wrapped. If it throws, the DB keeps the guests, no emails are sent, and a retry fails with emails_must_be_unique_valid.

verifier.reason: addGuests.handler.ts writes the new attendees with prisma.booking.update(createMany) (patch lines 516-530) outside any transaction, then calls eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees unwrapped (line 589), before the try/catch around sendAddGuestsEmails (591-595). Calendar API errors are swallowed in CalendarManager.ts:336-348, but updateAllCalendarEvents returns Promise.all(result) without await (EventManager.ts:920), so a rejected updateEvent escapes its catch. That happens if a CalendarService constructor throws in getCalendar, or credential.appId is read on an undefined credential (CalendarManager.ts:371). The guests then stay in the DB, no emails go out, and resubmitting the same guests hits emails_must_be_unique_valid (lines 498-505).

findings.claim: MultiEmail uses the array index as the React key, which misbehaves when items are removed from the middle of the list.

verifier.reason: MultiEmail does use `key={index}` (packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx, patch line 644), but each row is a controlled EmailField with `value={field}`. InputField only keeps its own state for `type=="search"` (packages/ui/components/form/inputs/TextField.tsx:98,142-148), so removing a middle item with splice re-renders the correct values and no row state ends up on the wrong item.

findings.claim: MultiEmail.tsx lives inside packages/ui but imports primitives from @calcom/ui, which also exports MultiEmail, creating a circular import risk.

verifier.reason: packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx:2 imports Button, EmailField, Icon and Tooltip from the "@calcom/ui" barrel, and packages/ui/index.tsx:153 re-exports MultiEmail from that same barrel, so the files do form a loop. The risk is small: MultiEmailLazy.tsx loads MultiEmail through next/dynamic, so the loop is not hit when modules first load. Many other packages/ui files already import from "@calcom/ui" this way, e.g. Checkbox.tsx:7 and AnimatedPopover.tsx:5.

findings.claim: The MultiEmail component reassigns its function parameter `value`.

verifier.reason: The new file packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx takes `value` as a destructured parameter at line 12 and reassigns it at line 14 with `value = value || [];`.

findings.claim: The MultiEmail component uses the useLocale() hook but lacks the 'use client' directive.

verifier.reason: The new packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx calls useLocale() (line 1 import, used inside the component) and has no 'use client' directive, while sibling form components such as packages/ui/form/PhoneInput.tsx have one. Its only consumer is the client-side AddGuestsDialog, which loads it through the next/dynamic wrapper in MultiEmailLazy.tsx, so nothing breaks today.

findings.claim: EventManager is built from ctx.user's credentials rather than the organizer's. References without a credentialId are matched against the caller's calendars when an attendee or owner adds guests.

verifier.reason: addGuests.handler.ts (patch lines 582-589) builds EventManager from `...user` and `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`, not from booking.user. In EventManager.ts:871-878, a calendar reference with no credentialId is matched only by type against `this.calendarCredentials` (the caller's). The other_calendar branch at 898-918 also uses the caller's credentials. So when an attendee or team owner adds guests, the update runs against their calendars instead of the organizer's.
